statement: BIS's rule 2024-28270 states that BIS is adding a new ECCN control on HBM stacks with a specific memory bandwidth density to ECCN 3A090.c.

citations.anchor: Based on the importance of HBM described above, BIS is adding a new ECCN control on HBM stacks with a specific memory bandwidth density to ECCN 3A090.c.

statement: The term 'HBM' with which rule 2024-28270 names the stacks it adds to ECCN 3A090.c is the alias of the Atlas's record High Bandwidth Memory, and names the same kind of part.
reasoning: The rule's sentence names 'HBM stacks'. The Atlas's working definition reads: 'High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) is a memory component: a stack of DRAM dies, placed vertically and connected directly by through-silicon vias.' The rule's word is the record's alias HBM, applied to stacks. 'With a specific memory bandwidth density' limits which stacks the entry covers; that is scope, which stays in the text, not a different class. The rule also defines its term at its edges (p.11: high bandwidth memory includes DRAM ICs whether or not they conform to the JEDEC standards, above its density threshold; co-packaged logic and HBM chips are not covered by 3A090.c), so the text's class and the Atlas's may differ at their edges; the link does not carry either edge. It concludes only that the two words name the same kind of part. It does not conclude that every member of the class, or any product or firm, is controlled, for which destination or under which licence policy, or that the control is in effect on any date (policy-links.md K-2, D-167).

statement: BIS's rule 2022-21658 states that BIS adds to the CCL certain advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment under a new ECCN 3B090; its amendatory text heads that entry '3B090 Semiconductor manufacturing equipment, not Controlled by 3B001'.

citations.locator: p.7, section IV, 'First, BIS adds to the CCL'
citations.anchor: First, BIS adds to the CCL certain advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment under a new ECCN 3B090, controlled for RS and AT reasons of control with limited license exception availability.
3B090 Semiconductor manufacturing equipment, not Controlled by 3B001, as follows

statement: The term 'semiconductor manufacturing equipment' that rule 2022-21658 uses for the equipment it adds under ECCN 3B090 is the name of the Atlas's record Semiconductor manufacturing equipment, and names the same kind of part.
reasoning: The rule's sentence names 'certain advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment', and the entry's heading 'Semiconductor manufacturing equipment'. The Atlas's working definition reads: 'semiconductor manufacturing equipment is the class of tools used to fabricate, assemble, test and package chips.' The words are the record's name; 'certain advanced' limits which tools the entry covers, which is scope, not a different class. It concludes only that the two words name the same kind of part. It does not conclude that every member of the class, or any product or firm, is controlled, for which destination or under which licence policy, or that the control is in effect on any date (policy-links.md K-2, D-167).

statement: BIS's rule 2023-23049 states that it removes ECCN 3B090 and replaces and expands its provisions in ECCNs 3B001 and 3B002, and that ECCN 3B090 was added to the CCL in the October 7 IFR.

citations.anchor: Principally, this rule removes ECCN 3B090 and replaces and expands its provisions in ECCNs 3B001 and 3B002.

citations.locator: p.17, section C.3 'Removal of ECCN 3B090 and Conforming Changes'
citations.anchor: BIS added ECCN 3B090 to the CCL in the October 7 IFR. This rule removes ECCN 3B090

statement: BIS's rule 2023-23049 states that it amends the EAR to implement SME controls more effectively, and that it removes ECCN 3B090 and replaces and expands its provisions in ECCNs 3B001 and 3B002.

citations.anchor: This IFR addresses comments received in response to only the part of the October 7 IFR that controls semiconductor manufacturing equipment (SME) and amends the EAR to implement SME controls more effectively and to address ongoing national security concerns.
Principally, this rule removes ECCN 3B090 and replaces and expands its provisions in ECCNs 3B001 and 3B002.

statement: The term 'SME', which rule 2023-23049 defines as semiconductor manufacturing equipment, is the alias and the name of the Atlas's record Semiconductor manufacturing equipment, and names the same kind of part.
reasoning: The rule's summary writes 'semiconductor manufacturing equipment (SME)' and then 'SME controls', the controls it implements. The Atlas's working definition reads: 'semiconductor manufacturing equipment is the class of tools used to fabricate, assemble, test and package chips.' The words are the record's name and alias. Which tools ECCNs 3B001 and 3B002 cover is scope, which stays in the text. It concludes only that the two words name the same kind of part. It does not conclude that every member of the class, or any product or firm, is controlled, for which destination or under which licence policy, or that the control is in effect on any date (policy-links.md K-2, D-167).

statement: BIS's rule 2024-28270 states that it amends ECCN 3B001, that seven commodities are moved from former ECCN 3B001 paragraphs into the new ECCN 3B993, and that ECCN 3B002 is amended by removing 3B002.b from certain license requirements in the license requirements table.

citations.anchor: This section discusses the amendments to ECCN 3B001 other than the commodities moved to new ECCN 3B993

citations.locator: p.17, section D.4 'Addition of ECCN 3B993', after the crosswalk table
citations.anchor: Seven commodities are moved from former ECCN 3B001 paragraphs into the new ECCN 3B993
ECCN 3B002 is amended by removing 3B002.b from certain license requirements in the license requirements table.

statement: BIS's rule 2024-28270 states that its changes to the EAR's controls include adding new controls for certain semiconductor manufacturing equipment and related items.

citations.anchor: makes changes to the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) controls for certain advanced computing items, supercomputers, and semiconductor manufacturing equipment, which includes adding new controls for certain semiconductor manufacturing equipment and related items

statement: The term 'semiconductor manufacturing equipment' that rule 2024-28270 uses for the items it adds new controls on is the name of the Atlas's record Semiconductor manufacturing equipment, and names the same kind of part.
reasoning: The rule's summary names 'certain semiconductor manufacturing equipment and related items'. The Atlas's working definition reads: 'semiconductor manufacturing equipment is the class of tools used to fabricate, assemble, test and package chips.' The words are the record's name; 'certain' limits which tools are covered, and 'related items' are not part of the link. It concludes only that the two words name the same kind of part. It does not conclude that every member of the class, or any product or firm, is controlled, for which destination or under which licence policy, or that the control is in effect on any date (policy-links.md K-2, D-167).
